lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.systemQubits
lean.annotation: In first quantization, each moving particle has its own momentum register. The 218 electron registers use $218\cdot3\cdot6=3{,}924$ qubits. The $\alpha$ particle adds $3\cdot8=24$ in `systemQubits`. The fixed proton positions are classical parameters of the Hamiltonian.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.Configuration
lean.plain: Proton positions and initial projectile momentum
lean.annotation: The proton positions $R_\ell$ are arbitrary real coordinates and enter the Hamiltonian through $S(\nu)=\sum_{\ell=1}^{216}e^{-ik_\nu\cdot R_\ell}$. The projectile offset is $k_{\mathrm{proj}}=2\pi p_0/\Omega^{1/3}$ for an integer vector $p_0$. Lean enforces $\|k_{\mathrm{proj}}\|_2\leq29{,}376$ a.u. with a bound on the squared norm. The projectile kinetic energy uses $k_p-k_{\mathrm{proj}}$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.IsGridState
lean.plain: Valid grid encodings and negative zero
lean.annotation: `IsGridState` checks each momentum coordinate of one basis index. The Hamiltonian applies this test to both indices, then compares their decoded integer momenta to determine the transfer. For example, an electron at coordinate 30 cannot be transferred by $+2$ in that coordinate, since 32 is outside the electron grid.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.hamiltonian
lean.plain: Discretized Hamiltonian on the plane-wave grid
lean.annotation: Lean tests both indices of $\langle x|H|y\rangle$ before evaluating the kinetic and Coulomb terms. The resulting matrix is $H_{\mathrm{grid}}\oplus 0$, so the ideal evolution is $e^{-iH_{\mathrm{grid}}t}\oplus I$. In particular, it preserves the valid grid subspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.IsGridState
lean.plain: Valid grid encodings and negative zero
lean.annotation: The sign bit and zero magnitude give two bit strings for zero. `IsGridState` removes $(1,0)$ in every coordinate, leaving one string per integer. Six qubits then give the 63 electron values from $-31$ to $31$, and eight give the 255 projectile values from $-127$ to $127$.

statements.markdown: The valid grid subspace excludes the signed-magnitude negative zero
